text:
Mattias Samuelsson is playing more than 23 minutes a night for a Buffalo team that has lost four straight, and the title of the team's video with him after the fourth loss said what you'd expect from a leader on a struggling team: "A Lot Of Hockey Left To Play." He is one of the Sabres' alternate captains and their workhorse on the back end.

The offense has gone quiet. After a 13-goal, 41-point season that Evolving-Hockey rated 20th among 215 defensemen, he has 2 goals and 11 points in 20 games, with none of those points on the power play and no goals in his last ten. His shooting and scoring rates are both close to what our numbers expect, so this looks less like bad luck and more like a smaller offensive role.

The defensive side has been mixed. Buffalo has had only about 48% of the chance quality at five-on-five with him on the ice, worse than without him. The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn pointed to him losing Frank Nazar down low on a Chicago power-play goal on Nov. 12. The minutes say the coaches still trust him. The results have to catch up.
headline: Mattias Samuelsson carries heavy minutes through a Sabres slide
